overview:
The chapter turns from lights and vessels to *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the supernal man, and shows from a person why even its outer vessels are still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. "From my flesh I see G-d": man is a microcosm, with every nature and with a connection to G-d above them all. His *yechida* and *chaya* are in no vessel, yet his will shines through *chachma* and *bina* into the heart, all at one shot.

The heart is *lev*, thirty-two, because the thirty-two chambers of the brain, four brains of eight each, are revealed in it; in the mind they are the fifty gates of *bina*, still hidden in understanding. For an emotion to be born the intellect must first go away, like a rotting seed, through the narrow of the throat, and only the *uvchein* comes over. Yet the heart never diverges from the mind, so to change yourself, change your understanding. Down to the breath in the lungs it is still one with the will, as G-d's simple will is in the heart of *Zeir Anpin*. Along the way: an eighth of an eighth of *gaava*, and the Chanuka oil.

departure: the intellect has to go away before the emotion can be felt
the narrow of the throat: the neck between brain and heart, where the intellect is channeled down to the uvchein
the membrane of air over the brain, which separates the koach hamaskil from the brain and brings it in as an idea

the impressed: the reflex of the emotion, the physical change it makes in the body
the breath of the chest: the lungs, the outer vessel of the heart, where the emotion and the will are felt
the will of the heart: the inner will of the yechida, like the pintele Yid, felt as the heart's yearning for good

sections.summary: After the long introduction on lights and vessels, the chapter turns to *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, the supernal man who receives from *Abba* and is the source of the life of the worlds. Like a person's body, which he controls and in which he feels his every desire, even its outer vessels still count as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

blocks.text: Chapter 32, on the heart. **Now** that the lights and vessels are done, we see why they were needed: we must understand the supernal man of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) **that sits on the chair, the throne**, *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) of *Atzilus*, which receives from the *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Abba* (*chachma* as a *partzuf*).

blocks.text: Still, **the body is still called the end of the world of the infinite**, still G-dly, **because G-d is one with the lights and with the vessels**. So it is the world of the infinite all the way to the external vessels of *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.text: As with a person's body: he controls even its outermost vessels, so their limit is only potential, and a desire is at once an impulse he feels, in his lungs or the like. Inwardly it is *mamash* (actually) one with him; outwardly it does whatever he wants. Both ways it is still infinite, the intermediary between infinite and limited: an "infinite ability to limit things into however he wants."

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Lights and vessels came first because the main vessels are those of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, whose *mashal* is the body: the soul is the light, the body the vessels. The soul has vessels even before the body, letters and *hagbalos* (limitations), but the main one is the body, which holds the soul's consciousness in a limited way and lets it deal with the world outside: *kelim* and *tikunim*, the two *inyanim* (matters) of the vessels. After the introduction on *gvul b'poel* and *gvul b'koach* (an actual limit and a limit in potential), he applies it to *Zeir Anpin*.

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin*, down to its external vessels, is still *Elokus* (G-dliness), the end of the world of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), because a ray of the *Kav* (the line of light) is still there. So in a person: your consciousness is felt in your body, your *ratzon* (will) is expressed in it, and you control it directly. Its limit is only *gvul b'koach*: your hand moves only in certain ways, but within that field you are unlimited. "It's *Ein Sof* within a very narrow, you know, field of movement."

sections.title: From my flesh I see G-d: man is a microcosm, and his chaya and yechida are in no vessel
sections.summary: The body explains *Atzilus* because man was made in G-d's image: every level of creation is in him, and he also has a connection to G-d higher than all of them, the two things free choice needs. In the soul, *chaya* and *yechida* encompass the intellect and the emotions and are in no vessel; only from *chachma* down is the soul drawn into a vessel.

blocks.text: **To explain this**: "from my flesh I see G-d." From the way our body works we understand the way the vessels of *Atzilus* work, because **man was made in the image of G-d**: "Let us make him **in our form, like our image**."

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Why the plural? G-d spoke to everything in creation, all the *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) and the whole *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), since every level is put into man; Rashi says to the angels, and they are the particular forms of the *hishtalshelus*. Man is a microcosm: "He has the whole world in him."

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: It need not be that the way it is in you is the way it is upstairs, "but that's what it says in the Torah." G-d did not have to do it that way, but as our *hishtalshelus* is set up and as our minds understand things, what is in you is upstairs. You are a *chelek Elokah* (a part of G-d) given a form through *tzimtzumim* (contractions); dig into yourself and you uncover that G-dly essence and see everything as it is in G-d and everywhere.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: In the depth, "all of the wellsprings connect." But a person is *mamash* a microcosm of every form in the world, and revealed: every type of animal and every angel is in him, while an animal has only a certain nature.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Penguins, hamsters and the black widow
blocks.text: This is one of the two things free choice needs: unlike an animal, a person has every nature at his disposal. Each animal has one. Emperor penguins care for their eggs and do a lot for them; they cannot help it, "it's not like they decided to have this self-sacrifice." Some fish eat their eggs as soon as they lay them, and only the survivors are born. Some fathers eat their young, "like Russian dwarf hamsters, I don't know, some of these kind of things or mice, I think," so you cannot keep them in one cage. The black widow is famous for eating her husband after they have kids. Some animals are faithful to their spouse, some are not, some kill their spouse.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: A person has all of them, nice and mean and the rest, and can choose whichever he wants. But having every nature is not enough: we also have the connection to G-d, higher than all the forms, the other reason we can choose. "You really need both": everything in creation, and a connection to G-d higher than creation.

blocks.text: **For we see** **in the soul of man** that his *chaya* and *yechida* (the two highest levels of the soul), his inner volition and his self, encompass his intellect, emotions and actions: *nefesh*, *ruach* and *neshama*. These levels are higher than any particular vessel or organ center.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: *Yechida* is the desire and the simple essential pleasure, in no particular vessel. And there is **the inner source of the intellect**, called *maskil* (one who has intellect): the *makif* (encompassing light) of *chaya*.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Both are **not limited to a specific vessel at all**. A person's inner self, expressed in desire and pleasure, and his creative intellect do not come from a vessel; they are spiritual levels of the soul. Their later expression goes through the body and can be explained biologically or psychologically, but the levels themselves cannot be predetermined or manipulated physically.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: *Chaya* is usually *ratzon*, but here it is the *pnimiyus* of the *sechel* (intellect), and *yechida* the *ratzon v'taanug pashut*, the simple will and delight. Deeper is the person himself, "the *yechida* without a name"; the *yechida* with a name is the pleasure of being himself and the desire to express himself. Neither is in a vessel.

audio.lecture: 71 - Chap- 32-1 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

sections.title: Thirty-two paths of bina: why the heart is called lev
sections.summary: The brain has four parts, *chachma*, *bina*, and *daas* divided into *chesed* and *gevura*, and each has eight chambers: thirty-two, the thirty-two paths of *bina*. The heart, *lev* (thirty-two), is where they are revealed as emotion; in the mind they are the fifty gates of *bina*, still hidden in understanding like kindnesses covered within *Ima*, until they come out as love in the heart.

phrases.en: from the 32 chambers that are in the brain,

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: which are called the 32 paths of *bina*,

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: that open up,

phrases.en: The mind is divided into four parts.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Now a little into the heart: **from the 32 chambers that are in the brain**, called the *lamed-beis shvilin* (the thirty-two paths) of *bina*, **that open up** to become the brains, the intellect, of the emotions. What are the thirty-two chambers of the mind?

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **The mind is divided into four parts**, and physically the brain has four parts to match. In front is the cerebrum, the main thing, plainly two hemispheres, "the right and the left brains"; behind it the smaller cerebellum, the back brain. Right and left are *chachma* and *bina*; the cerebellum is *daas* (knowledge), including the medulla oblongata, where the brain turns into the spinal cord, the intermediary between the brain and the nerves of the body.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The cerebellum is really two brains too: *daas* divides into *chesed* (kindness) and *gevura* (might, restraint), and physically it is two hemispheres, only attached much more tightly, so it looks like one. The cerebrum's halves are separate, joined by the thing in the middle.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: "Just for the record": everything in the middle that connects is *daas*: what joins the two hemispheres, the whole back brain, the medulla oblongata, the extensions to the eyes, ears and other senses. The medulla connects the intellect to the body, the cerebellum is the actual thinking of *daas*, and the *daas elyon* (higher knowledge) connects *chachma* and *bina*. So the brain has four parts: *chachma*, *bina*, and *daas* divided into *chesed* and *gevura*.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: וכל אחד יש בו ח' חדרים,
phrases.en: and each one of these four brains has eight chambers.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: which is 32.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And **each one of these four brains has eight chambers**: four times eight, **which is 32**. Each has all four within it, *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura* of *chachma*, and each of those goes up into the theory and down to the application: *chachma* and *Yisroel Saba*, *bina* and *tevuna* (the sides of *chachma* and *bina* that go to the application).

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: The eight corners of a sukka
blocks.text: Like a *sukka*, a cube: four corners on top and four on the bottom. The top four are the letters of *Havaya*: *yud* *chachma*, *hei* *bina*, *vav* *chesed*, *hei* *gevura*. The bottom four are *alef*, *dalet*, *nun*, *yud*, the Name *Adnus*. Eight chambers in each brain, times four: "so really you have 32 brains in your brain," and each divides further, infinitely.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Whenever you think, these thirty-two are working. A new idea starts as a flash in *chachma* of *chachma*, and then, "this is like the way the brain works," the electrical and chemical signals go bouncing from brain to brain: to *bina* to think about it, back for an emotion, whether you like the idea, back to think more, down to an application, up to its source, until it comes out as a particular train of thought.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Doing it goes down the spine, but thinking about doing it needs the bottom of the brain: *daas*, and *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*, a *chachma* and a *bina* for the practical, and then a practical *chesed* and *gevura*. Eight chambers in each of four brains: thirty-two.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: and this is why your heart is called a heart in Hebrew.

audio.lecture: 72 - Chap- 32-2 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: An eighth of an eighth of pride
blocks.text: "And this is by the way a very important, but slight digression": a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar) has to have *shminis sheb'shminis*, an eighth of an eighth, a sixty-fourth, of *gaava* (haughtiness). Of the explanations, one fits here: the brain divides into thirty-two brains, and the heart reveals those thirty-two emotionally.

blocks.text: That is the *pnimiyus* of the heart, itself called a brain, because you understand a thing more fully when you experience it: pick the chamber, put it in your heart, and you feel it as if it were real. So there are sixty-four brains, and for a *talmid chacham* one of them has to be a brain of *gaava*; the other sixty-three are in *anivus* (humility) and *bittul* (self-nullification).

blocks.text: Which one? "The top one." All the brains are you understanding and interpreting what the Torah said, or what your *rebbe* taught you. But the point you start from has to be with *gaava*: that is what it says, that is the truth, "and I'm not telling you my opinion." Your job is to teach, explain and interpret, but you have no jurisdiction to compromise what the Torah says when you give it over.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's advice before a debate
blocks.text: The Rebbe advised Rabbi Hollander, "he came and spoke for us once," who was to debate Reform and Conservative rabbis. blocks.text: Recap of the way from the mind to the heart. The mind has four parts: in front *chachma* and *bina*, the two hemispheres of the cerebrum; in back the brain of *daas*, the cerebellum, which looks like one but is two closely attached hemispheres, the *chesed* and *gevura* of *daas*, by which you call an idea good or bad. Each has eight, like a *sukka*: *chachma*, *bina*, *chesed* and *gevura*, each going up to the theory and down to the practical (*Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*, chapters one and two). Eight times four: the thirty-two paths of *bina*.

blocks.title: A path through the woods
blocks.text: The *shvilin*, pathways, are how it breaks through, like the Red Sea split into twelve *shvilin*, "you know, like when the Rebbe would come through 770 and make a *shvil*." A *shvil* is not a road or a *derech* (a way) but a path through the woods, through grass and trees and bushes, "this little break." Normally the brain will not connect to the emotions, but through these thirty-two paths, the *uvchein* ("and so": the conclusion that applies the idea to me), it comes across into the heart and is felt. That is why it is called *lev*.

blocks.title: The disinterested law student
blocks.text: Or in law, you try to be "disinterested, not uninterested": interested, if you are to succeed, but with no emotional stake in the outcome; objective, impartial. So you treat it as an intellectual issue: what do ownership, property, liability mean, where do they extend, how do they apply? You can conclude that something is good or bad, that somebody is guilty, yet it stays a little removed from emotion. Translate it to a case relevant to you, "Well, that means that you don't really own your house," and you will get emotional. That is different.

blocks.text: *Mesirus nefesh* means making it the top priority. "Well, we have the oil anyway, so we'll use it" is not *mesirus nefesh*. *Mesira* is giving yourself over: "I'm committing to do this no matter what." "Simple words, you know, no romanticism." I commit to put on *tefillin*: it costs money, I don't care; it takes time, I don't care; somebody wants to kill me, I don't care; somebody says I am *mevatel* (wasting) time from Torah, I don't care. It can even be for a bad thing: it only means everything else is secondary, and whatever contradicts it, big or small, counts for nothing.

blocks.title: The Alter Rebbe in jail
blocks.text: Even in *ruchniyus*. When the Alter Rebbe was in jail they told him, "You have to eat, or else you'll be killing yourself," and lose your *olam haba*, if he refused the non-kosher food. *Al pi Torah* (according to the Torah) one could get a *heter* (permission); but if you believe the world is here for *Torah* and *mitzvos*, and that is its *teva*, you may expect a miracle when you try to do a *mitzva*. Besides, some opinions allow it, and "that's not such an example": the danger was not certain or immediate, and even halachically it is not such a big question. With such an attitude, as the Rebbe said about the Frierdiker Rebbe, "you know you're going to win."

Another: nothing in *kedusha* (holiness) can contradict another thing in *kedusha*; if you think one will lessen your ability to do another, you are mistaken: either it is not really *kedusha*, or it will not really mess you up.

sections.title: The intellect must go away before the emotion: the rotting seed and the narrow of the throat
sections.summary: An emotion that is only implicit in understanding can be born in the heart only after a *tzimtzum* and a *histalkus*: the intellect has to go away, as a seed rots before it grows. That is the *meitzar hagaron*, the narrow of the throat between brain and heart, one of three partitions in the body, with the membrane over the brain and the diaphragm.

phrases.en: and behold,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: ודאי כאשר צריך להיות התהוות התפעלות המדה בלב
phrases.en: surely when the emotion has to be created, when you actually want to feel something in your heart,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: מן העלם התפעלות המדה בהיותה בשכל והשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: It's going to be coming from the hidden excitement of the *midda*, the way that it's in your intellect and the understanding of *bina*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: הוצרך להיות תחלה בחינת צמצום והעלם וכיווץ שנקרא הסתלקות
phrases.en: Before you can have the emotion, you have to first have a *tzimtzum*, a *helem* and a *kibutz*: the idea has to be focused down to a *uvchein*, the *sechel* has to be hidden, and the light has to be removed. This is called a *histalkus*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And **surely when the emotion has to be created**, felt in the heart, it comes from the hidden excitement of the *midda* (attribute) in the intellect and understanding of *bina*, already implicit there: you understood that this thing is bad for you, but did not yet feel it.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Would you turn on the light for me on Shabbos?
blocks.text: A person learns *hilchos Shabbos*: this is an *issur d'oraisa* (a Torah prohibition), this an *issur d'rabbanan* (a rabbinic one), this *mutar* (allowed), this *patur* (exempt), and for this they stone him. Implicit is a *midda* not yet revealed: that it is bad, against what G-d wants, and he would be scared to do it; in the time of the *beis din* (the court) he would get *skila* (stoning). Because he understands, it comes out by itself when somebody says, "Dude, would you turn the light on for me on *Shabbos*?" He would be scared; he would not. Even with something little, a *d'rabbanan*: "You want to hand me that stone?" "No, it's *muktza*."

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: So **before you can have the emotion, you have to first have a** *tzimtzum* (contraction), a *helem* (concealment) and a *kibutz* (gathering): the idea is focused down to a *uvchein*, the *sechel* hidden, the light removed. This is a *histalkus* (departure): the *sechel* has to go away.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: like the *mashal* of the rotting of a seed,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: in order to change from one thing to another,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Like the *mashal* of the rotting seed: **in order to change from one thing to another**, from physical to spiritual, it has to rot; the original contradicts the new and has to go away. So while a person is focused on the intellect, the emotion cannot come out: the intellect has to go away for him to really feel.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: "This is one of the reasons why women get more emotional, because they're *kalei daas*" (of light mind). Little children too are more emotional, while a mature person, especially a *bar sechel*, a real intellectual, has emotions always subdued and cold: he is always thinking of things intellectually.

blocks.text: While a person focuses on the intellect, the emotions are quiet; when he is very emotional he is not rational. But only in *chitzoniyus*, with a *chitzoniyus'dik sechel*; with a *pnimiyus'dik sechel* they come together. "That's the rule for anything," a *klal gadol* (a great rule): whenever *Chassidus* says two things differ, one higher and one lower, go deep enough and there is a level where they connect.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: this is the idea of the narrow of the throat,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: when it goes into the narrow of the throat of *bina*, the excitement of the intellect goes away,

phrases.he: ונמשך להיות בשינוי המהות בהתפעלות הלב
phrases.en: and then it becomes changed and it becomes an excitement, emotional excitement in the heart.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: So **this is the idea of the narrow of the throat**, the *meitzar hagaron*: from brain to heart you go through the neck, and its narrowness shows physically that it has to be focused and channeled smaller, and that the brain stops.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: This fits last week's *parsha* (Torah portion) too: the throat's *kaneh*, *veshet* and *veridin*, windpipe, food pipe and jugular vein, the three *simanim* (signs) of *shechita* (ritual slaughter), match the three officers, the *sar hamashkim*, *sar ha'ofim* and *sar hatabachim* (the chief butler, baker and slaughterer). "So, that's just a little living with the time there."

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **When it goes into the narrow of the throat of** *bina*, **the excitement of the intellect goes away**, and it is changed into an emotional excitement in the heart. In the mind you are excited by the understanding; in the heart, by the *uvchein*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Tell me why I should care
blocks.text: In the mind there is the beauty of the idea, how great the explanations were: after a good *shiur* (class), a person is excited mainly by how well it was explained and that he understood something new. Others say, "Okay, but why do I care? It was very nice, you explained all this stuff, but who cares? Tell me why I should care." "That's the heart speaking." The intellect wants to know just to know; the heart wants to know how I fit in the picture. That is the *uvchein*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Is G-d giving me money, or the stock market?
blocks.text: So the *sechel* goes away and you feel only the *uvchein*. In a *beis din* the man does not want the reasoning, only whether it is his money. So with *Chassidus*: your heart wants to know, "Okay, so at the end of the day, you know, is G-d giving me money or is the stock market giving me money?" Should I be afraid? How should I react to the world? This is a *memutza* (a middle) or a *masach* (a screen).

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: this is similar to the *kruma d'avira*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: שהוא המעלים ומפסיק מכח עליון שלמעלה מן השכל, לבוא לשינוי המהות בגלוי אור השכלה כו'
phrases.en: The *kruma d'avira*, the membrane of air, separates between the *koach hamaskil*, which is higher than intellect, and changes it so that it should come into the brain as an idea, as a *sechel*.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: וכמו חצר הכבד שמפסיק ומבדיל בין אברי הנשימה לאברי המזון
phrases.en: and like the *chatzar hakaved*, the partition of the liver, which is the diaphragm, the muscle underneath the lungs, that separates between the organs of breathing, the cardiovascular system, and the organs of digestion, the digestive system,

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: so that it should change from an emotion to a physical thing.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: like explained elsewhere at length.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **This is similar to the** *kruma d'avira* (the membrane of air). Three *parsaos* (partitions) in the body separate the *Chabad*, the *Chagas* (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*) and the *Nehi*. The *kruma d'avira*, over the brain, takes the liquid from the *koach hamaskil* and the *taanug* into the brain as *hevel* (vapor): what is higher than intellect becomes an idea. The *meitzar hagaron* turns a *sechel* into a *midda* by letting only the *uvchein* come over. The *chatzar hakaved*, the diaphragm, turns an emotion into a physical impulse, to run away or to do something.

audio.lecture: 75 - Chap- 32-5 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: And like the *chatzar hakaved* (lit. the partition of the liver), the muscle under the lungs that separates breathing from digestion, **so that it should change from an emotion to a physical thing**. A scared person has to go to the bathroom. Why? The emotion changes his breathing, the diaphragm's rhythm pushes on the stomach, and the digestive system shuts off and empties itself, so he can run away better, without spending energy on the food or carrying its weight. As explained elsewhere at length.

sections.title: The heart follows the mind exactly, all the way to the breath of the chest
sections.summary: Though the emotion changes its nature, it never diverges from the understanding: the heart needs the mind to tell it where to go, so the way to change yourself is to change your understanding. The emotion is a whole *partzuf*, its thought, its feeling and its reflex, and even its outer vessel, the breath in the lungs, is still one with the will: still *Ein Sof*.

phrases.en: nevertheless

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: המדות שבלב הן בדומה ממש אל המדות שבשכל, ממש כאופני התפעלותם במוח, בלי נטיה כקוצו של יו''ד
phrases.en: your *middos* are exactly according to your understanding, and it doesn't even diverge by the tiniest drop.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Though it changes from intellect to emotion, **your** *middos* **are exactly according to your understanding**, not diverging by the tiniest drop. The heart never runs off on its own; it does not know where to go and needs the mind to tell it. Once told, it runs farther than the mind would: "All right, it's a good thing, all the way good... That's it, I love it, I'm going to go do it." The mind: "Oh, wait a minute, wait a minute." The heart: "Too late, you already told me it's good, I'm going." It may get irrational, but never with an emotion different from your understanding.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: A basic premise of *Chabad Chassidus*: since *mo'ach shalit al halev*, the mind controls the heart, and your actions follow your emotions, go to the root and change your understanding; then how you feel and how you act change by themselves. "So that's the best way to change yourself."

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: רק שבלב באין בשינוי המהות ובהגבלה וצמצום דבחינת נצח והוד דבינה,
phrases.en: only that in the heart it gets changed and becomes limited through the *tzimtzum* of *netzach* and *hod* of *bina*, which is the idea of the *uvchein*,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: שהוא שליחות שפע אור ההשגה בעצם, בשביל התפעלות המדה לבד כידוע
phrases.en: this is when the mind is figuring out how should I react based on this idea.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **Only that in the heart it gets changed and becomes limited** through the *tzimtzum* of *netzach* (victory) and *hod* (acknowledgement) of *bina*, the *uvchein*: **this is when the mind is figuring out how should I react based on this idea**, the *tevuna* explained before, only the *chitzoniyus* of the *sechel*.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: ובמדות שבלב כלול מג' מדריגות, חב''ד חג''ת נה''י
phrases.en: and when a person has the *midda* in their heart, it also has a full *partzuf* of *Chabad*, *Chagas*, *Nehi*,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת המושכל ומורגש ומוטבע הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like we explained in the last chapter, that there's the intellect of the emotion, the feeling of the emotion, and the natural impulse or reflex of the emotion,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: וג' כלים לכל אחד, פנימית ואמצעית וחיצוניות כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: and each one, the *muskal*, *murgash* and *mutba*, has three *kelim*: inner, middle and outer, explained at length in the last chapter.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: The *midda* in the heart is itself a full *partzuf* (lit. face; a stature of the *sefiros*) of *Chabad*, *Chagas* and *Nehi*, as the last chapter explained: **the intellect of the emotion, the feeling of the emotion**, and its reflex, the effect it has on you; the *muskal*, the *murgash* (the felt) and the *mutba* (the impressed).

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.title: Somebody punches you
blocks.text: Somebody punches you. The *muskal* is thinking why you are excited: "Oh, he punched me, I'm so..." The feeling is getting all hot, "like you breathe fire from your nose", breathing heavy and quick, heart pumping, blood boiling, turning red. The *mutba* is the reflex, the physical change: your muscles tense up, which is part of how you feel it, getting your body ready to run away or to fight.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: "I mean really it's like getting... it's really gets a person ready to kill somebody." Nowadays it is tamer, but the emotion is for the extreme: if he is dangerous, get rid of him. Fear runs away; anger wants to kill the person. "Maybe it doesn't come out that far because you don't want to get arrested or whatever, but really that's what the emotion wants to do."

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **And each one**, the *muskal*, the *murgash* and the *mutba*, **has three** *kelim* (vessels): **inner, middle and outer**, as explained at length in the last chapter: three times three is nine.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בחינת החיצוניות דכלים דנה''י שבלב
phrases.en: but even the external vessels of the *Nehi* of the heart,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: - שהוא בחינת התפעלות החסד והאהבה שבלב כשבאה לידי השפעה לחוץ, שנקרא נה''י דחזה
phrases.en: which is the excitement of the heart when it comes, like a *chesed* and love, to outside, in the *Nehi* of the chest, of the lungs,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: in thought, speech and action.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: היינו על ידי חיצוניות הכלי דלב,
phrases.en: this is through the external vessel of the heart, which is the lungs,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: which is the thing that makes the emotion sink in, or the reflex of the emotion,

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: אשר בהבל החזה דזעיר אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: which is in the breath of the chest of *Zeir Anpin*.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד
phrases.en: that about this it says, *ihu v'garmohi chad*.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

phrases.en: It's its own way of *Ein Sof*, meaning that it's still, like in the *mashal*, under your control.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: **But even the external vessels of the** *Nehi* **of the heart**: the *Chabad* of the emotion is in the right side of the heart, the *Chagas* in the left, and the *Nehi* in the lungs. The excitement of the heart, love and *chesed*, comes out in the *Nehi* of the chest, the lungs, **in thought, speech and action**: the lungs become a vessel to make you think, speak and do.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: Most obviously in speech: you hear the emotion in the voice. But thought too gets an emotional background from how fast you breathe, which changes oxygen levels and the like: "you can have different tones of voice within your own thoughts, also." Fast breathing makes fast thinking, a rushed feeling. And in action: a happy person does things light, relaxed, bouncy; an angry one is tense and jerky, mainly from the change in how fast he breathes.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: This is through the outer vessel of the heart, the lungs: the *mutba*, the reflex by which the emotion sinks in, in the *hevel hachaze* (the breath of the chest) of *Zeir Anpin*; your breathing changes with your emotions. Of this it says *ihu v'garmohi chad* (He and His organs are one): the emotion reaches the outer vessel of the *Nehi* of *Zeir Anpin* straight from the intellect, and that straight from the *ratzon* and *taanug*. Your mood, your breathing, how tense you are, all connect back to your will: "So it's *mamash* one." It is still *Ein Sof* in its way, still **under your control**; you are still a *ba'al bechira* (one with free choice) over it.

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

blocks.text: That is why your mental state affects your physical health: anger is bad for the heart, because it changes how the heart and lungs work, "and that's why they say laughing is good for you." The same in the *nimshal*; "well, let's first do the *mashal*."

audio.lecture: 76 - Chap- 32-6 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA .mp3

sections.title: The mashal and the nimshal: the will felt in the heart, and G-d's simple will in the heart of Zeir Anpin
sections.summary: In a person the essential will shines through the intellect into the heart and is felt in the breath of the chest: the *re'usa d'liba*, the heart's yearning for good, one with the will at one shot. So too in *Zeir Anpin*, the heart of G-d's conduct of the world: whether *vayomer el libo* or *vayisatzev el libo*, it is G-d's simple will from before the *tzimtzum*, and so all of it is still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's hand-washing
blocks.text: Asked why he washed his hands a certain way, three times or something on each, the Rebbe Rashab said: "I don't know why, but I trained my body to always follow *Shulchan Aruch* exactly, and so I know that if my body does it that way, then that's the way you're supposed to do it. There must be a reason." In a way that is even more than what we are discussing here.

audio.lecture: 77 - Chap- 32-7 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA  (End).mp3

blocks.text: Here it is the *pintele Yid*: everybody has an inner feeling, from the inner *ratzon*, to be connected to G-d, to do good and go away from bad. Maybe his *sechel* does not understand it, so he lacks the *kelim* to be conscious of it, or he convinced himself it is not *shayach* (relevant) to him. But ever since he was a little kid he wanted to be a good, holy guy, like Moshe and Avraham, even if he never learned about them.

blocks.text: And **this is like a comparison to understand the supernal man**, **which is the idea of** *Zeir Anpin* **of** *Atzilus*: the *chitzoniyus* of the way G-d conducts the world, whose *pnimiyus* is the inner thing behind the *mitzvos*.

blocks.text: Of the heart of *Zeir Anpin* it says *vayomer el libo*, **Hashem said to His heart**, of the *Mabul* (the Flood). How G-d runs the world, the *chitzoniyus* of the heart, whether a flood to destroy everybody, "or he decides to, you know, recently we had these hurricanes and stuff," comes straight from the *etzem ratzon* (the essential will): it goes through *hishtalshelus* and *sechel*, but He chose it because He wanted it.

blocks.text: In **the external vessel of** *netzach* **and** *hod* **of the heart**, the impulse to give *brachos* (blessings) or, G-d forbid, the opposite, like the *Mabul*, shines the simple essential will of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* (the Essence of the infinite light) from before the first *tzimtzum*. G-d *mamash* controls it, so scientists cannot figure the world out as a system: "it's not a system." Look carefully and it grows more and more uncertain, until it is just a *ratzon*.

audio.lecture: 77 - Chap- 32-7 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA  (End).mp3

blocks.text: It is *mamash* a revelation of G-d's inner *ratzon*, by the inner plan for the *dira b'tachtonim*, open miracle or not; the question is only whether you see it. "Really nature is a miracle that happens over and over again. That's all." You think it is normal and miss G-d *mamash* doing whatever He wants, "and there is no rules." It never runs by the rules; a miracle just lets you see it.

audio.lecture: 77 - Chap- 32-7 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA  (End).mp3

blocks.text: This is the simple essential *ratzon* of chapter 10, **in** *Yachid*, *Echad*, *Kadmon* (single, one, original), **in the** *mashal* **of the person's inner desire for kindness**: one who *b'etzem* (essentially) has a *chafetz chesed* (a desire for kindness) feels in his heart to help when he sees a poor person.

blocks.text: So all the way to the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus* is still the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*: G-d's conduct of the world, whether He gives *hashpaa* (flow), money and food, or not, is still controlled by Him, and openly so.

audio.lecture: 77 - Chap- 32-7 Hamshacha from AvA to ZA  (End).mp3

blocks.text: That is **because He and His organs are one**, **just like in the person**: his inner *ratzon* and his heart are one *mahus* (what a thing is in itself), each expressing the other exactly: the *ratzon* goes down into the heart, and the heart's feeling goes all the way up to the *ratzon*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why are even the external vessels of *Zeir Anpin* still called the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, and what does a person's body show about it?
What two things does a person have that give him free choice, and how do the animals' natures show the first?
How do four brains with eight chambers each make thirty-two, and why is the heart called *lev*?
Why must the intellect go away before the emotion is felt in the heart, and what do the rotting seed and the *meitzar hagaron* show?
If the emotion changes its nature, why is the best way to change yourself to change your understanding?
What is the *re'usa d'liba*, and how does it show that the heart and the essential will are one?
